articles.title_orig: Watch 4 Songs From Goodspeed's The Snow Goose, Including Ally Bonino Singing 'The World Don't Want to Know'
articles.title_zh: Watch 4 Songs From Goodspeed's The Snow Goose, Including Ally Bonino Singing 'The World Don't Want to Know'
articles.content_orig:
Ashlyn Maddox, Eric Graise, Bonino, and more star in the world premiere musical version of Paul Gallico's 1940 novella.
October 02, 2026 By Andrew Gans
Goodspeed Musicals' world premiere of The Snow Goose is currently playing the East Haddam, Connecticut, venue through October 18. Watch Ally Bonino sing "The World Don't Want to Know" from the new musical, which began performances August 28, in the video above.
Adapted from Paul Gallico 's 1940 novella, the musical was 
commissioned by the Goodspeed, and is written by Jonathan Larson Grant 
winners Scott Gilmour and McKenzie. Marshall Pailet ( Private Jones )
 is directing. The story follows a young man and woman who together 
rescue a wounded snow goose on the coast of England in the months before
 World War II, spawning a transformative friendship as the boy sets off 
to save soldiers trapped at Dunkirk.
The cast features Eric Graise ( Tracker , Step Up: High Water ) as Philip Rhayader, Ashlyn Maddox ( Parade ) as Frith, Sam Sherwood as The Bard, Charlie Webb ( Parade , The Notebook ) as Wilf, and Bonino ( Suffs ) as Harper. The ensemble comprises Alan Chandler, David Aron Damane ( The Queen of Versailles ), Matthew Davies, Leah Hofmann ( Mrs. Doubtfire ), Kiersten Kelly ( Jurassic World: Chaos Theory ), Amy Hillner Larsen ( Once Upon a One More Time ), Sophia Anna O'Brien, Gabriel Marcus Omlor, Ayanna Nicole Thomas ( Harry Potter and the Cursed Child , How To Dance in Ohio ),
 Patrick Tombs, and John Viggiano, with swings Sam Hoffman and Eleni Kontzamanys rounding out the company. Casting is by Geoff Josselson Casting.
Below, watch highlights from three other songs: Graise singing "I Owe It to Myself," the company performing "I Come Back to You," and Maddox singing "That Were Some Day."
The musical also has choreography by Misha Shields , music 
direction by Adam Souza, puppet design by Nicholas Mahon, scenic design 
by Emmie Finckel , costume design by Mallory Kay Nelson, lighting design 
by Aja M. Jackson , sound design by Jay Hilton, and wig, hair, and 
make-up design by J. Jared Janas and Cassie J. Williams. Chris Zaccardi serves as production stage manager, with Talleri A. McRae as access 
consultant and Emily Reutlinger as associate director.
Tickets are available at Goodspeed.org .

articles.title_orig: Novartis strikes up to $7.8 billion mRNA deal with China's Abogen
articles.title_zh: Novartis strikes up to $7.8 billion mRNA deal with China's Abogen
articles.content_orig:
Novartis has signed a deal worth up to $7.8 billion, in the latest of a flurry of tie-ups between Big Pharma and Chinese biotechs.
The Swiss pharma major is entering a licensing agreement with China-based Abogen Biosciences for its lead asset, an early-stage experimental treatment for autoimmune disease, Abogen said in a statement on Friday.
China offers Western biopharma companies hopes of finding their next blockbuster drug, as patents on top-selling drugs, which generate hundreds of billions in sales, face a "patent cliff" in the early 2030s.
Novartis' normally stable shares fell last month by the most since 1987 following several clinical trial setbacks , raising questions about its ability to develop and source new drugs to offset the looming patent expirations.
As part of its Abogen deal, the company will pay $575 million upfront for the global rights to the Chinese company's messenger RNA therapy, with an additional $7.2 billion in milestone payments. It will also have the exclusive option to license Abogen's assets developed on its RNA platform.
Licensing deals have emerged as the preferred way for Western drugmakers tapping Chinese science, allowing them to buy the rights to experimental medicines without acquiring the companies that developed them.
Sidley partner Ruchun Ji told CNBC that such agreements can reduce risk for Big Pharma because licenses can be terminated if a drug disappoints or development priorities change. For Chinese biotechs, meanwhile, upfront and milestone payments provide a source of funding while allowing them to continue developing drugs in their home market.
"The speed of innovation, speed of clinical trials in China is really, really fast," Ji said, attributing the development largely to regulatory reform by China's drug regulator NMPA, which has "totally overhauled the systems over the last couple of years."
Combined with the return of Chinese scientists trained abroad, faster and cheaper early-stage clinical development helped the country's biotechs generate the data needed to attract the biggest biopharma companies in the world, he added.
Novartis' announcement comes after Danish weight loss drug maker Novo announced earlier this week an exclusive licensing agreement with Hengrui Pharma for an early-stage, once-weekly GLP-1/GIP pill for as much as $2.6 billion.
Novo, whose shares have plummeted over the past two years amid intensifying competition in the anti-obesity space, is under pressure to find a successor to its semaglutide franchise, which includes mega-blockbusters Wegovy and Ozempic.
The U.K.'s GSK said in mid-September that it was acquiring a blood cancer medicine from Chinese Chimagen Biosciences for up to $750 million.
GSK's head of business development, Chris Sheldon, told a London healthcare investor event last month that, while the company isn't targeting specific geographies for innovation, China's share of new biotech innovation is rapidly increasing.
ING has estimated that China will account for about a third of all new molecules in pharma companies' pipelines globally in 2026, up from 4% in 2014.
The bank expects the value of Chinese biotech outlicensing deals to surpass $250 billion in 2026, as overseas demand for its drug assets rises.
Drugs developed in China are increasingly being pulled into global Big Pharma development programs.
AstraZeneca early Friday announced it had entered a partnership with Summit Therapeutics to test its oncology drugs.
With Daiichi Sankyo, they will test AstraZeneca's cancer treatment Datroway in combination with Summit's ivonescimab, developed by Chinese biotech Akeso and licensed to Summit, across multiple types of tumour.
AstraZeneca has committed to investing $15 billion in China through 2030 to expand both manufacturing and research and development there. It has struck several licensing deals with Chinese biotechs exceeding a potential value of $1 billion in the past few months.

articles.content_orig:
The itineraries of previous trips reveal the image the country wants to project – eco-friendly, multicultural and hi-tech
China is ramping up its efforts to bring young Americans to China, and ready to be seen as a country concerned with environmental protection, lifting people out of poverty, protecting minority cultures and building the technology of the future.
That builds on an earlier target announced in 2023 that set the goal of bringing 50,000 US youth people to China by 2028, which the authorities said they had reached ahead of schedule.
The Young Envoys Scholarship (YES) initiative was launched to support this target. It is run by the China Education Association for International Exchange, a non-profit organisation under the Ministry of Education.

articles.title_orig: Cornell case latest: Gov. Hochul, special prosecutor hold press conference over gang rape allegations
articles.title_zh: Cornell case latest: Gov. Hochul, special prosecutor hold press conference over gang rape allegations
articles.content_orig:
• New York Gov. Kathy Hochul said she is “deeply disturbed” with the original investigation conducted by Cornell police following gang rape allegations at the Chi Phi fraternity house in 2024, vowing to unravel the investigation’s failures. “I will not allow anyone to sweep this case under the rug,” Hochul said at a news conference.
• Attorney General Letitia James, who will be taking over as special prosecutor in the case, said there is now “an active criminal investigation .” Cornell University said it supports the governor’s decision to assign the case to the New York Attorney General’s Office.
• Hochul also said she supports closing a “loophole” in New York law that can make it nearly impossible for survivors to seek justice if they voluntarily consumed alcohol or drugs before an assault.
Editor’s Note: This coverage contains some graphic and disturbing descriptions of sexual violence. For help in the US, call the National Sexual Assault Hotline at 1-800-656-4673 or chat 24/7 on online.rainn.org .
Cornell University issued a statement Friday expressing support for a change in New York law that would update the sexual assault statutes and make it easier to prosecute cases if a victim was voluntarily intoxicated.
Sex crime survivor advocates and experts often refer to a legal “loophole” in New York’s — and other states’ — sexual assault laws, which can make it nearly impossible for survivors to seek justice if they voluntarily consumed alcohol or drugs before an assault.
“If someone is too intoxicated to consent, it should not matter whether they chose to use drugs or alcohol,” New York Gov. Kathy Hochul said at a news conference today. “Voluntary intoxication is not a license for sexual assault or gang rape, period.”
Lawmakers in New York have for years tried to make changes to the law, but the bill has failed to move through the State Assembly for a full vote.
“We don’t know enough, but what is coming out beyond what everyone was told initially, or … two years ago, it is very contradictory and conflicting,” New York Gov. Kathy Hochul said during Friday morning’s news conference about gang rape allegations at a Cornell University fraternity house in 2024.
“I want the truth. I think every parent in this state, every New Yorker, wants the truth in this case, and that is why Attorney General James will be the one who puts a spotlight on this case,” Hochul said.
The governor said state Attorney General Leticia James, who will be taking over as special prosecutor in the case, will be the one to ask questions such as, “Who knew what when?; “What did they do wrong?”; “Why didn’t they come forward?”; and “How was this woman denied justice?”
Hochul said she has “every confidence” in James “to get it right.”
The attorney for Jane Doe in the alleged Cornell University gang rape case says Tompkins County District Attorney, Matthew Van Houten, tried to throw his client “under the bus.”
“He goes out and files his press release, basically throwing my client under the bus,” attorney, Thomas Giuffra, told CNN’s Pamela Brown on The Situation Room, adding that Van Houten implied Jane Doe’s sexual encounters had been consensual. “So I had a real issue with this district attorney.”
Giuffra said the district attorney reached out shortly after the civil lawsuit was filed, wanting Doe to testify before a grand jury in October.
“I paused when I heard that because look: I’m an experienced trial lawyer. I’ve tried well over 150 cases in my life. I couldn’t prepare a case in a month and do a good job in presenting it,” Giuffra explained. “So that raised the question in my mind.”
The attorney for Jane Doe in the alleged Cornell University gang rape case says his client is “not doing well.”
“She’s under siege on social media, where people are trying to identify her; some false court postings, attempting to identify her,” attorney Thomas Giuffra told Pamela Brown on CNN’s “Situation Room.”
Jane Doe has also received “overwhelming support of people all over the world,” the attorney said. Messages of support, which he has shared with his client, “really helped to know that she’s not alone because throughout this process, she felt like she was alone,” he said.
Cornell University has changed its answer explaining what information the school shared with the local district attorney’s office about Jane Doe’s allegations.
Cornell is named as a defendant in Doe’s civil lawsuit , which claims the school failed to adequately respond to Doe’s report of an alleged gang rape at a fraternity house in October 2024.
On Tuesday, Cornell launched an FAQ page to answer frequently asked questions from the media and public. The questions include:
Did Cornell Police adequately investigate the incident? Why didn’t they bring in the Ithaca Police?
Cornell initially said campus police “investigated the matter in 2024 and shared all investigatory information with the Tompkins County District Attorney’s Office,” according to a Wednesday morning screengrab of the page kept by CNN.
But by Friday, a different answer appeared under the same questions. It said Cornell police “investigated the matter in 2024 and shared the victim’s sworn statement and the Snapchat screenshot with the Tompkins County District Attorney’s Office.”
The change came after CNN’s repeated requests for clarification about what materials were handed over to the district attorney’s office.
The nuance is important because Cornell and the district attorney’s office are under scrutiny over what information the school shared with prosecutors and whether Doe’s complete accusations were reflected.
Earlier this week, the district attorney said an initial, signed statement from Doe that Cornell police provided to his office described events that did not constitute a crime. But Doe made a more explicit accusation of rape in an interview with Cornell police, which was documented in a transcript, according to CNN affiliate WCBS . The district attorney told CNN on Wednesday that his office never received that transcript.
New York Gov. Kathy Hochul said it’s time to change the state’s sexual assault law, which excludes victims who willfully became intoxicated.
“If someone is too intoxicated to consent, it should not matter whether they chose to use drugs or alcohol,” Hochul said Friday morning. “Voluntary intoxication is not a license for sexual assault or gang rape. Period.”
As CNN previously reported , activists and some lawmakers have pushed for this change for years, to no avail.
But Hochul vowed to help ensure the law changes as soon as possible.
“I support closing this loophole and will work with the New York State Legislature to accomplish this,” she said.
New York Gov. Kathy Hochul said Jane Doe was was repeatedly failed by the same institutions that were meant to protect her and argued that newly surfaced reporting has raised questions about information the Tompkins County DA relied on when deciding not to pursue any charges.
“This young woman had already endured something that is utterly unspeakable, and that at every turn she was failed by people and institutions with an obligation to protect her,” Hochul said during Friday morning’s news conference.
Hochul appointed state Attorney General Letitia James as special prosecutor, saying she will conduct a fresh investigation and pursue criminal charges should the facts warrant one.
“No institution gets to protect its its reputation at the expense of a young person seeking justice,” Hochul said. No public official gets to “look the other way when the system breaks down and fails our young people,” she said.
In a statement to CNN Thursday evening, Cornell said the university “supports Governor Hochul’s decision to assign this case to the New York Attorney General’s Office.”
New York Gov. Kathy Hochul declined to say whether Cornell’s president or the Tompkins County district attorney should step down at this time saying she conveyed her “deep concern” over the handling of the case to the univer

articles.title_orig: Taylor T-Shirts Impact Lives Through Partnership with World Orphans
articles.title_zh: Taylor T-Shirts Impact Lives Through Partnership with World Orphans
articles.content_orig:
Lydia Wilhelm 02 October 2026
Would it really be a prospective student visit without a free t-shirt? If you see a student walking backwards across campus giving a Taylor tour, you’re bound to see some visitors with classic Taylor purple t-shirts hanging over their arms. However, you might not know that this common prospective student gift is creating uncommon change in the lives of Guatemalan families through Taylor’s partnership with World Orphans .
World Orphans is a non-profit organization with a vision of relational healing and financial independence for families who have been separated due to poverty or abuse. One of the ministry arms within the organization is the World Orphans Market , an economic empowerment program. This program equips women with sewing skills, and these women are then employed as artisans to return to them the dignity of meaningful work and financial freedom. All of World Orphans’ work is grounded in a Christ-centered philosophy of human worth: everyone is created with intrinsic dignity and with a God-given purpose. Additionally, World Orphans works through local churches, ensuring that these women are supported by Christ-centered communities as they work their way out of poverty and towards better lives for their families.
Like so many Taylor stories, Taylor’s journey to partnering with World Orphans is a story of community. When the Admissions team connected with World Orphans, they saw an opportunity—an opportunity for Taylor as an organization to model the same mission it seeks to foster in its student body. Taylor always has a need for t-shirts—particularly in Admissions. Here, Taylor’s tangible need for shirts meets these Guatemalan women’s tangible need for living-wage work, creating a true, mutually beneficial partnership.
As the Admissions team collaborated with World Orphans’ Guatemalan team, they encountered some community connections that made one thing clear—God had already been opening doors for this partnership. One of these connections was Lily Sachsenmeier ’26, who finished her Orphaned & Vulnerable Children degree interning at World Orphans in Guatemala, where "a highlight was getting to talk with social workers at World Orphans who support local families, empowering parents with education and resources to care for their children. I was really moved by the personal experiences they shared and by their passion for their work."
During her time in Guatemala, Sachsenmeier also had the opportunity to meet some of the artisans making the t-shirts for Taylor Admissions, bringing this community story full circle.
Reflecting on Taylor’s choosing World Orphans to supply their next batch of Admissions t-shirts, Sachsenmeier said, "I’m deeply touched that Taylor is partnering with World Orphans. As a student, I got many free t-shirts for events and programs, and I’m so glad that Taylor is being intentional about where they source some of these t-shirts. I’m incredibly proud that Taylor is investing in t-shirts made by these women in Guatemala as part of World Orphans’ economic empowerment program!"
At Taylor, a t-shirt is so much more than a clothing item—it’s a walking billboard for who we are. It says, "I believe in what goes on here." Now, Taylor purple has additional purpose. These t-shirts are a physical manifestation of our mission to "minister Christ’s redemptive love, grace, and truth to a world in need." They are a reminder of a God who opens doors. And a reminder of what a true partnership can look like.
Learn more about how Taylor equips students to break cycles of vulnerability through our Orphaned & Vulnerable Children major.

articles.title_orig: Ken Urker, partner of Gypsy Rose Blanchard, found dead in Louisiana home
articles.title_zh: Ken Urker, partner of Gypsy Rose Blanchard, found dead in Louisiana home
articles.content_orig:
Ken Urker, the partner of Gypsy Rose Blanchard, was found dead at his  Louisiana home Thursday evening, authorities said.
Deputies responded to a home in Raceland around 6:15 p.m. and found Urker dead, the Lafourche Sheriff’s Office said in a statement.
“At this time, we are continuing the death investigation,” the office said.
The cause of death has not been revealed. But Blanchard, who welcomed a daughter with Urker in 2024, told People magazine that he overdosed. The magazine reported that he died on his 34th birthday.
The sheriff’s office did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Blanchard said she was in “disbelief.”
“I can’t think,” she said. “I’ve screamed until my throat burns.”
The couple met through a pen pal program while Blanchard was in prison for her role in the 2015 murder of her mother Clauddine “Dee Dee” Blanchard, Variety reported . The pair briefly split and then reconciled in 2024.
Blanchard, has said her mother abused her for years and forced her to fake serious illnesses. She pleaded guilty to second-degree murder and was sentenced to 10 years in prison. Her then-boyfriend, Nicholas Godejohn, was sentenced to life in prison for fatally stabbing Dee Dee Blanchard.
The killing sparked a media frenzy and inspired HBO’s 2017 documentary “Mommy Dead and Dearest” and the 2019 Hulu series “The Act.” Blanchard was released early in 2023 after being granted parole .
She told People that Urker was heavily scrutinized during their relationship.
“Ken endured an unimaginable level of public scrutiny and relentless cyberbullying across social media platforms, including TikTok and Reddit. The cruelty directed toward him was something no human being should have to endure,” she said in her statement. “I believe the tremendous weight of that scrutiny and harassment had a profound impact on him, and I hope his passing serves as a reminder that there is a real person behind every screen, every headline, and every comment.”
She said she wants their daughter to grow up “knowing how deeply her father loved her and who he was beyond what strangers on the internet chose to say about him.”
The Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration has a 24/7 National Helpline for individuals with substance abuse issues and their family members. The hotline, which offers assistance in English and Spanish, can be reached at 1-800-662-HELP (4357). To find behavioral health treatment services, visit SAMHSA’s website .
Minyvonne Burke is a senior breaking news reporter for NBC News.

articles.title_orig: Rolls-Royce Opens World’s First “Black Badge Lounge” in Beverly Hills
articles.title_zh: Rolls-Royce Opens World’s First “Black Badge Lounge” in Beverly Hills
articles.content_orig:
Rolls-Royce debuts the world’s first Black Badge Lounge in Beverly Hills, complete with a hidden speakeasy and private customization atelier.
by Michael Van Runkle – October 02, 2026
Just off Rodeo Drive, in the heart of Beverly Hills last night, Rolls-Royce held an exclusive opening for a new dealership featuring the world’s first “Black Badge Lounge.” The Great Gatsby-themed soiree within a tastefully updated studio featured live music, flapper dancers, champagne towers, and Dalmore 17 scotch whisky cocktails, giving loyal customers and media a chance to experience the showroom floor, visit the speakeasy in the rear, and then venture upstairs to the “Black Badge Atelier” that offers a private escape for speccing highly personalized Rolls-Royce motorcars.
The crisp white walls with contrasting vertical bars so reminiscent of Rolls-Royce’s iconic front grilles perfectly mirrored a 1925 Phantom “Round Door” that the nearby Petersen Automotive Museum kindly contributed to the evening’s festivities. This first-generation Phantom received custom coachwork in 1934 from Jonckheere, in Belgium, and retrospectively represents the first iteration of the Black Badge ethos that Rolls-Royce brought to life officially in 2016.
Parked diagonally across the showroom floor, a Spectre Series II embodied the very opposite end of the spectrum, with a fully electric powertrain that proves exactly how well prodigious silent power matches the modern luxury experience – especially in Black Badge form.
“Black Badge has always been about a different side of Rolls-Royce,” Director of Sales & Brand Julian Jenkins told duPont REGISTRY. “One that is bolder, more contemporary, and a little unexpected. After ten years, it felt like the right moment to give that spirit a home of its own.”
The new Beverly Hills dealership will operate as part of the broader O’Gara Coachgroup , at the heart of Los Angeleno car culture with showrooms full of McLaren , Bugatti , Koenigsegg , Pininfarina , Aston Martin , Lamborghini , and Rimac nearby. Tom O’Gara himself greeted customers and friends at the opening, before handing the microphone over to a jazz ensemble. As the music played, guests circled through the Black Badge Lounge to an outdoor area where a team of torcedores hand-rolled cigars.
Upstairs in the Atelier, out of sight from the main floor and bar, a private experience for speccing and customizing Rolls-Royces hinted at the nearly countless options available for sumptuous leathers, plush high-pile carpets, contrast stitching threads, and more – all rendered digitally in real time on a large screen to complete the immersive experience.
“The Atelier lets people step into the Black Badge world, more than just seeing it in a motorcar,” Jenkins continued. “It doesn’t feel like a conventional showroom, it’s a more relaxed, considered environment in which clients may spend time, explore ideas, and begin to imagine something entirely their own. Of course, we are consistently seeing ever greater interest in personalization and one-off creations, and the Atelier offers a more engaging and inspiring way for clients to begin that commissioning journey.”
The new dealership drew a healthy showing from across the broader Los Angeles cityscape, especially the next generation of luxury consumers emerging out of the tech industry, social media, and creative fields. As the initial introduction for new customers, or reestablishing a familiar foundation for existing owners, the world’s first Black Badge Lounge aims to create a level of direct engagement that sets the proper tone for ownership of the world’s finest motorcars.

articles.title_orig: McMinnville siblings earn karate medals around the world
articles.title_zh: McMinnville siblings earn karate medals around the world
articles.content_orig:
MCMINNVILLE, Ore. (KPTV) - Logan and Kenzie Mendonca, a brother and sister from McMinnville, are competing in karate tournaments around the world.
“We are more stressed watching each other fight than when we are competing ourselves,” Kenzie said.
The siblings have traveled to multiple countries to compete.
“Canada, Mexico, Chile, Brazil, Paraguay, Costa Rica,” Logan said.
“I think Africa, just to make one,” Logan said, referring to places they haven’t competed.
Logan and Kenzie recently returned from Guadalajara, Mexico, with Youth League Karate gold medals. Their medals hang in the family dojo, the Mendonca Academy of Martial Arts in McMinnville.
“It’s a place of calm. I come in here and my problems are outside,” Logan said.
The siblings have competed in karate since they were three years old. Their father, Tony, leads their training routine.
“You learn time management, you learn how to get your things done because the dojo isn’t something that you can skip. It is a mandatory part of your routine,” Kenzie said.
“Just traveling and seeing crazy stuff but also winning and losing together is something really special to me,” Logan said.
Logan and Kenzie competed at the Junior Pan American Karate Championships in San Jose, Costa Rica. Logan won the Junior Male title in his fifth appearance at the event.
“I went bronze, silver, silver, then I took fifth and this year I won, so this year was my first year winning, pulling it out. It was my third year in the finals,” Logan said.
Logan is ranked No. 1 in the U.S. and is a senior at McMinnville High School. Kenzie, a sophomore, won Pan American Cadet Female silver for a third straight year.
“I think the most-cocky part of it for me is being in three finals before Logan,” Kenzie said.
“Yeah, I mean her record is better than mine,” Logan said.
“On paper if you look at like our ages my stuff looks cooler than his,” Kenzie said. “Because I’m better earlier.”
Both Logan and Kenzie were named team captains for the United States. They will next compete at the Junior World Championships in Poland.
“He’s Spiderman but when he comes home, he’s Peter Parker,” Kenzie said.
Logan is a National Merit Scholar semifinalist with aspirations of attending college in France to study physics.
“Right now Peter Parker has national merit, but nobody knows he’s Spiderman and nobody cares,” Kenzie said.
Logan and Kenzie will miss about nine days of school for the trip to Poland. They are completing tests during lunch breaks and will bring homework with them.

articles.title_orig: Mid-Michigan musicians complete 60-hour-long jam session, breaking world record
articles.title_zh: Mid-Michigan musicians complete 60-hour-long jam session, breaking world record
articles.content_orig:
What makes a good jam session? Maybe it’s the combination of instruments or the vibe of the music.
For a group of Michigan musicians this week , they cared less about the quality and more about how long they could play for what they believe is a record-breaking jam session.
The world record attemp t started Monday at 10 a.m. with six musicians on stage at UrbanBeat in Old Town Lansing, Michigan. Jeff Boog helped organize the jam.
"We are doing a continuous musical collaboration for three days without doing what humans normally do, which is to stop and take a break, change the subject, go do something else," he said.
There's no official Guinness World Record for longest jam, so Boog and his friends settled on going beyond the longest nonstop improvised music session they could find: 57 hours played in Spain in 2024.
They set a few rules for themselves to make the challenge more structured: like having at least three musicians on stage at all times, keeping everything improvised with no planning ahead of time and, most importantly, the music never stopping.
But they weren’t going to do it alone, so they recruited more than a hundred other musicians, from professionals to amateurs to anyone who just wanted to play, to swap out in shifts for the marathon jam. There were guitars, clarinets, bongos and a tuba on stage at various points among other instruments.
By 7 p.m. on Tuesday, more than halfway through the jam, dozens of musicians had taken the stage, many of them meeting for the first time. One of them was singer and guitar player Mary McGuire.
"I think I just played with three different drummers, probably seven or eight guitar players, two different bass players," she said. "The piano player was great, and then a woman jumped up and was singing harmonies."
Another participant, Zachary Mead said collaborating like this isn’t as hard as you might think
"People that play music, they kind of just they figure it out," Mead said. "They start playing and then they figure it out."
With no way to really know how the jam would go before they started, organizer John K. Addis was happy to see how everyone had come together.
"They are jamming constantly. There are no covers, no pauses, and somehow it's all working," Addis said. "I don't think we've had a pause more than like five seconds."
The group crossed the 57 hour mark with a countdown Wednesday night, breaking the record set in Spain, but the music didn't stop just yet.
3 hours later at 10 p.m. and after 60 straight hours of playing, the musicians finally put down their instruments.
UrbanBeat owner Terry Terry, who had hopped on stage a few times throughout the jam to play flute and percussion, made this declaration:
"We set out to prove that Lansing is the music capital of Michigan, and I think we're now the jam capital of the world," Terry said.
Organizers say they plan to submit their performance to Guinness with hopes that it will be officially recognized, and that they’re ready to come back if anyone else decides to jam out longer.
Additionally, the jam has inspired new ideas for the Lansing music scene including creating more dedicated nights for musicians who've never met to collaborate together.

articles.title_orig: Uzbekistan dominates chess Olympiad while England’s Sivanandan, 11, sets new world age record
articles.title_zh: Uzbekistan dominates chess Olympiad while England’s Sivanandan, 11, sets new world age record
articles.content_orig:
Host nation won having led almost from start to finish, while young English player reached a stunning landmark
Uzbekistan, the host nation, won the open gold medals at the 2026 Olympiad, the biennial chess international team tournament, at Samarkand last week in the style of the legendary Soviet grandmasters of long ago. India, the defending champions, were second, Germany a surprise third, and the top-seeded United States fourth.
The hosts led almost from start to finish, with world No 5 Nodirbek Abdusattorov and the world title challenger Javokhir Sindarov their top-board powerhouses. The team recovered swiftly from a single defeat by Germany, and were particularly impressive in crushing Armenia by 3.5-0.5 in the penultimate round. The Uzbekistan government rewarded each of the five players with $200,000 (£178,000), a house and a Volkswagen, plus $50,000 for the coach Rustam Kasimdzhanov.
India performed in line with their seeding. Putting the world champion, Gukesh Dommaraju, on board four boosted his results but also underlined that Sindarov is the favourite for the coming world championship match. Gukesh was exposed in the final rounds when he was outplayed against both Germany, although he won that game fortuitously, and Hungary.
The final leading scores were: Uzbekistan 20/22 match points; India and Germany 18 ; USA, Azerbaijan, Armenia and Hungary 17 ; China, France, Spain, Ukraine and England 16 (206 teams competed).
England’s creditable 12th place, one below their seeding, would have been higher still if a third player had performed at the level of the nine-time British champion Michael Adams, 54, and the Spectator chess columnist Luke McShane, 42, who were both in contention for individual medals right up to the final round. England’s women were 15th against their seeding of 20th, and the combined performance was the best since at least 2018, and probably since 1990.
Russia/USSR, which monopolised Olympiad golds in the second half of the 20th century, have been banned from the last three competitions due to the invasion of Ukraine. If allowed to take part, a team of Ian Nepomniachtchi, Andrey Esipenko, Daniil Dubov, Vladislav Artemiev and Alexander Grischuk would have been contenders.
The potential of Turkey’s Yagiz Kaan Erdogmus stands out. The 15-year-old won the individual silver medal unbeaten and has advanced to No 17 in the live ratings, a similar level to Bobby Fischer at that age and well ahead of current world No 1 Carlsen when he was 15. Here he defeats a rival prodigy , Argentina’s Faustino Oro.
China won the women’s Olympiad ahead of Kazakhstan, India and the US, and did so with its B team. World champion Ju Wenjun, world No 1 Hou Yifan, former title challenger Tan Zhongyi and world No 3 Lei Tingjie all stayed at home, but their substitutes, led by world No 4 Zhu Jiner and 16-year-old Lu Miaoyi, proved highly effective.
For the future, the US is potentially a powerhouse in women’s chess. Its duo of Carissa Yip, 23, and Alice Lee, 16, are both targeting the open GM title and its $100,000 bonus offered by Dr Jeanne Cairns Sinquefield, while new candidates are emerging in Rachael Li, Rose Atwell and Zoey Tang who are all teenagers with 2300+ ratings.
Bodhana Sivanandan broke the world age record for the youngest ever woman grandmaster (WGM). Her 8/11 total, playing all games with no rest days, included six wins, draws against Ukraine’s reigning European champion Anastasiia Hnatyshyn and Georgia’s former World Blitz champion Nana Dzagnidze, both of them current world top 20 players, and a solitary loss to Deysi Cori of Peru due to a time-pressure blunder in a drawn ending.
The 11-year-old Harrow schoolgirl’s record as the youngest ever WGM broke Hou’s 2006 mark by several months, and she also recorded her second norm (of three needed) for the international master (IM) title at open level. For IM, she also needs a 2400 rating against her current 2382, which includes the Olympiad.
Her last-round Olympiad game was a model of what has become her trademark style of a Magnus Carlsen grind.
If she secures her final norm and becomes an IM before her 12th birthday, she will break the all-time female No 1 Judit Polgar’s world age record and also become one of the 10 youngest ever IMs. She is already No 2 among all players born in 2015, behind only Russia’s IM Roman Shogdzhiev, who has been groomed for several years as a potential heir to Anatoly Karpov.
after newsletter promotion
The Guardian’s Matthew Weaver interviewed Sivanandan after her return home. At the end of the Olympiad the youngster talked with Lichess.org’s Theo Wait , while chess.com also covered her achievements in detail .
The Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport’s new £250,000 a year Supporting Elite Chess Fund document contains no specific provision for rewarding world-record breakers. Maybe it should, as Sivanandan’s IM title and new record could follow as soon as the London Classic, which begins in November.
Sivanandan has just started at secondary school, and that could slow her progress on the chessboard. The advance from IM to GM is difficult, and many talents eventually plateau, which should temper extrapolations of a rise comparable to Polgar and Hou.
Meanwhile Timur Turlov, 38, a Russian-born entrepreneur from Kazakhstan whose company Freedom Holding has a multibillion dollar valuation on the Nasdaq index, was elected as the new president of the world chess body Fide last Saturday.
The previous Fide President, Russia’s Arkady Dvorkovich, had planned to run for a third term but was forced to withdraw due to EU sanctions on his assets and travel visas.
Turlov received 96 votes against 76 for the German businessman Wadim Rosenstein and a surprisingly low 20 for the ticket of Jan Henric Buettner of Freestyle Chess and the ECF’s international director Malcolm Pein. In the run-off ballot they switched to Turlov, who defeated Rosenstein 110-85.
Turlov is young, committed and with proven business skills. However, there could be an immediate problem since Rosenstein has appealed to the court of arbitration for sport over the new president’s eligibility.

articles.title_orig: EXCLUSIVE: Europe weighs new diesel stocks release after US pressure, sources say
articles.title_zh: EXCLUSIVE: Europe weighs new diesel stocks release after US pressure, sources say
articles.content_orig:
Oil prices were lower on Friday, extending losses from earlier in the session, following reports of a potential move to release additional diesel and crude stocks to ease a global supply shortage.
Brent crude futures, international benchmark, with December expiry traded down 2.6% at $99.65 per barrel, while U.S. West Texas Intermediate futures with November expiry fell 4% to $89.11.
It comes shortly after Reuters reported that European Union member states were discussing a French proposal to release additional diesel reserves following pressure from the Trump administration .
The report, which cited a single unnamed source familiar with details of the discussion, said France had proposed that EU nations release 50 million barrels of diesel and International Energy Agency members release 50 million barrels of crude oil.
CNBC could not independently verify the report. A spokesperson for the French government and the IEA were not immediately available to comment.
The EU is holding crisis talks on Friday to discuss a coordinated response to soaring diesel prices after U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent called on European countries to urgently release some of the continent's reserves.
In a post on social media, Bessent said Thursday that America's European partners "should accelerate delivery on their existing commitments and make additional supplies immediately available to address ongoing disruptions."
He added: "American farmers, truckers, and businesses should not be left carrying the burden of a global diesel shortage."
U.S. President Donald Trump , who has repeatedly touted the prospect of a diesel export ban, appeared to cool on the idea earlier this week, following a resurgence in crude exports through the strategically vital Strait of Hormuz.
The U.S. supplied around half of the EU's diesel imports in August, according to the International Energy Agency, underscoring the 27-nation bloc's exposure to a potential export ban.
Oil prices settled higher in the previous session amid a report that the U.S. is sending a third aircraft carrier strike group to the Middle East, along with an amphibious force carrying 2,000 Marines, raising the stakes for an escalation in the months-long conflict.

articles.title_orig: 2026 Right Livelihood laureates challenge autocracy, patriarchy, and AI bias
articles.title_zh: 2026 Right Livelihood laureates challenge autocracy, patriarchy, and AI bias
articles.content_orig:
The 2026 Right Livelihood Award is honoring women and women-led organisations confronting the world ’ s most entrenched power structures: authoritarian rule, patriarchal violence, and unchecked AI development.
Their common thread is resistance to systems that push people to the margins, and a shared insistence on putting people back at the centre.
The 2026 Right Livelihood Award, also known as the “ Alternative Nobel Prize, ” has been awarded to Jalila Haider from Pakistan “ for breaking barriers, as the first female lawyer from her Hazara community, to challenge ethnic, state and patriarchal persecution, guided by the conviction that no human being is illegal,” the Rural Women ’ s Assembly “ for organising rural women across Southern Africa into a united force defending land, seed, and bodily autonomy against corporate and patriarchal dispossession,” the Georgian Young Lawyers ’ Association “ for building and safeguarding Georgian democracy and sustaining civic power in the face of an autocratic crackdown,” and Timnit Gebru from the US “ for challenging concentrated power in artificial intelligence and pioneering digital technology rooted in justice, lived experience and human agency.”
World Council of Churches general secretary Rev. Prof. Dr Jerry Pillay commended the women honored. “ These Right Livelihood laureates exemplify the kind of empowerment that is life-flourishing, deep-rooted, and of the people,” he said, adding a special congratulations to the Rural Women ’ s Assembly from his home country of South Africa. “ I have seen firsthand the power of volunteers who can put the region ’ s food systems back into the hands of resilient people and communities.”
For over 45 years, the Right Livelihood Award has honoured and supported people leading the way to a just, peaceful, and sustainable world for all.
The 2026 awardees were chosen from 200 nominees from 72 countries. They will be honoured during a televised award presentation in Stockholm on 1 December.

articles.title_orig: CALENDAR UPDATE: MÉRIDA JOINS THE FIM MOTOCROSS WORLD CHAMPIONSHIP AS THE NEW HOME OF THE MXGP OF SPAIN
articles.title_zh: CALENDAR UPDATE: MÉRIDA JOINS THE FIM MOTOCROSS WORLD CHAMPIONSHIP AS THE NEW HOME OF THE MXGP OF SPAIN
articles.content_orig:
ERNÉE (France) 2 October 2026 – Infront Moto Racing is proud to announce that Mérida, the capital of Extremadura, will join the FIM Motocross World Championship in 2027 as the new home of the MXGP of Spain on 17-18 April . Alongside the MXGP and MX2 World Championship classes, the weekend will also host rounds of the EMX250 and EMX125 European Championships , bringing the full spectrum of international motocross to one of Spain's most historic destinations.
The arrival of Mérida is part of a wider project for MXGP in Spain. Both Spanish events on the calendar, the MXGP of Spain in Mérida and the MXGP of Andalucia will be delivered by the same organisers, Seventy 6 Motion . Bringing both events under one partner creates a single, coherent vision for the championship in Spain, built on three pillars: stability, growth and innovation.
Each event is secured under a three-year agreement starting in 2027 and running until the end of the 2029 season. This long-term commitment gives riders, teams, partners and fans a clear horizon in a nation that has celebrated many World Champions in recent seasons, including Guillem Farres, current MX2 World Champion and Daniela Guillen, 2026 WMX World Champion; and which now looks ahead to the next generation of Spanish talent ready to fight for the title on home ground.
WHERE HISTORY MEETS MOTOCROSS
Founded in 25 BC as Augusta Emerita, Mérida became the capital of the Roman province of Lusitania and today preserves one of the most important Roman archaeological ensembles in the world. The Roman Theatre, Amphitheatre, Circus, Temple of Diana and Roman Bridge are among the landmarks that have earned the city its status as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
The arrival of MXGP creates a unique connection between an ancient Roman capital and the energy, speed and spectacle of modern motocross, with more than 2,000 years of history forming the backdrop to a brand-new chapter for the championship.
A CITY OF CULTURE, TOURISM AND MAJOR EVENTS
Events such as the International Classical Theatre Festival and Emerita Lvdica have shown Mérida's ability to transform its historic setting into a stage for major national and international occasions, experience that will now be put to work for the world's premier motocross championship. Mérida is now turned to the future with development in its accommodation capacity and annual programme of major events continuing to grow.
The region itself of Extremadura also offers spectacular natural landscapes, open countryside, historic cities, renowned gastronomy and a strong connection with outdoor life, making it a natural fit for a sport rooted in the land.
Its location also gives the event an important cross-border dimension. Mérida sits on the Madrid to Lisbon and Seville to northern Spain transport corridors, placing the new venue within easy reach of fans from across Spain and neighbouring Portugal. Badajoz Airport is approximately 50 kilometres away, while Seville and Lisbon provide additional international gateways.
David Luongo, CEO & President of Infront Moto Racing: "Not long ago it was difficult to have races in Spain, and the Spanish Federation and the whole motocross community there have done fantastic work since. This year Spanish riders won three titles, in the European classes, in WMX and in MX2. The MXGP of Andalucia had one of the biggest crowds of the season, with an organiser and a region that truly embrace motocross. As promoter it is important to develop the Spanish market, and I am sure every Spanish rider is very happy to have a second race at home. We have no doubt it will be a success."
Antonio Alia Portela, FIM/CMS Director: "Organising one MXGP event is crazy enough, and these people are going to organise two in Spain! They showed us this year in Almonte, in the middle of one of the most protected natural areas in Spain, that they are capable of something unexpected and very successful. Now they bring us to Mérida, which the Romans named Emerita Augusta and planned as one of the most important cities of the empire. It is another special place, close to the Portuguese border, and I know it is going to be really, really successful. For the community, there will not only be motocross but also a spectacular city to discover."
Juan Cabral, Strategics Director Seventy 6 Motion : " The arrival of MXGP in Mérida presents an extraordinary opportunity to showcase Mérida and Extremadura on the international stage, blending over 2,000 years of history with the excitement and spectacle of the world's best motocross.For Seventy6 Motion, this Grand Prix also marks a significant milestone in a project founded with the aim of creating and developing major motorsport events capable of generating a positive impact on the region—sporting, tourism-related, and economic alike. We want to build a Grand Prix in Mérida with a unique identity, one that grows and establishes itself firmly on the global calendar. We extend our special thanks to Infront Moto Racing for the trust they have placed in us, as well as to all the institutions and organizations making this project a reality.
On April 17 and 18, 2027, a new chapter begins for Mérida, for Extremadura, and for Seventy6 Motion. We want the world to discover that here, where history spans more than two millennia, we can also write the future of motocross."

articles.title_orig: Dow jumps 400 points after weak jobs data sends yields tumbling: Live updates
articles.title_zh: Dow jumps 400 points after weak jobs data sends yields tumbling: Live updates
articles.content_orig:
Stocks jumped Friday, as yields retreated following a surprisingly weak jobs report that raised hopes the Federal Reserve will hold rates steady in October.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 323 points, or 0.6%. The S&P 500 gained 1.1%, while the Nasdaq Composite climbed 1.7% to a new all-time high.
Treasury yields fell Friday, with the 10-year yield dropping 2 basis points to 5.216%. The 2-year yield was flat after initially sliding following the employment report. One basis point is equal to 0.01%, and yields and prices move in opposite directions.
Tech stocks rallied as risk-taking resumed on Wall Street, with shares of Nvidia hitting an all-time high for the first time since May. CrowdStrike , Palo Alto Networks and AMD also all rose to all-time highs. Meanwhile, shares of Intel and AMD also jumped more than 4% each.
September's nonfarm payrolls report showed the U.S. economy added 29,000 jobs last month, with unemployment rising to 4.2%. The Dow Jones consensus called for jobs growth of 84,000 and for the unemployment rate to hold steady at 4.1%.
"This is the exact kind of number the market wanted from a labor standpoint," said Phil Blancato, chief market strategist at Osaic. "Not too hot, not too cold ... not overly great, and not weakening."
That number made traders reassess the next move for the Federal Reserve. Fed funds futures trading suggests an 86% likelihood the central bank will stand pat at this month's meeting, up from a roughly 76% chance just the prior day, according to the CME FedWatch Tool.
Saira Malik, chief investment officer at Nuveen, told CNBC's "Squawk Box" that the report may give the market support before earnings season kicks off, which she thinks will be "very strong."
"So, I think this could be the start of the Santa Claus rally that we've all been hoping for," she said.
Oil prices dropped sharply from their highs, supporting equities, following a report that European nation states are considering a release of strategic fuel reserves following pressure from the Trump administration.
Investors are coming off a modestly higher session Thursday, to start off the month of October. However, the Dow and the S&P 500 were headed for weekly losses amid a global bond rout, while the Nasdaq was the only major average on pace to end the week with gains.
— CNBC's Jeff Cox contributed to this report
Nvidia popped on Friday, briefly hitting an all-time intraday high.
Shares of the semiconductor firm rose more than 3% to as much as $237.88 on the day. At its peak, the stock traded at its highest intraday level ever.
Nvidia's shares began trading on the public market in January 1999.
Revisions in the September jobs report for July and August are making those months look weaker for job creation.
July was marked down by 31,000 to mark a net job loss of 10,000 on the month, the Labor Department reported Friday. August was marked down by 29,000 for a new total of 133,000 compared to the initial robust report of 162,000.
"Revisions made both July and August look weaker, too. Over the past 3 months, we've an average of a mere +17k per month," economist Justin Wolfers wrote on social media .
Stocks opened higher Friday.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 322 points, or 0.6%. The S&P 500 gained 0.8%, while the Nasdaq Composite climbed 1.1%.
The latest fed funds futures trading showed an 86% likelihood that the Federal Reserve will hold rates steady when it convenes for its Oct. 27-28 meeting, according to the CME FedWatch Tool. That's up from a roughly 76% chance just one day prior.
The U.S. economy added 29,000 jobs and the unemployment rate increased to 4.2 percent in September as job creation slowed substantially during the month, the Labor Department reported Friday.
Economists were expecting 84,000 new payrolls and the unemployment rate to hold steady at 4.1%.

Shares for Seagate Technology and Western Digital slipped over 10% and 8% respectively after Toshiba announced plans to double its production capacity for hard disk drives used in data centers, according to a Nikkei report.
The Japanese company plans to invest $380 million to expand facilities in the Philippines, signaling Toshiba's first major hard disk drives investment in about five years, Nikkei reported.
Toshiba, along with Seagate Technology and Western Digital, are the top competitors in the hard disk drives market.
Morgan Stanley put Nvidia back atop its list of semiconductor stocks on Friday, touting the company's range of customers and the importance of graphics processing units (GPUs) to agentic artificial intelligence.
"While 90% of investor conversations are around the biggest hyperscalers and frontier model companies, half of the business - probably the faster growing half - is a broader range of AI model companies, Neoclouds, sovereign entities, ODMs and OEMs, and enterprise customers," Joseph Moore at Morgan Stanley wrote in a Friday note to clients.
Moore has an overweight rating on the stock with price target of $300 and an "industry view" listed as "attractive."
With its numerous backstopping and vendor agreements during the AI boom, Nvidia has faced criticism for being involved in circular financing during the AI buildout, which interlinks Nvidia's investments with its eventual revenue streams.

Moderna will replace Warner Bros. Discovery in the tech-heavy blue-chip Nasdaq 100 index after the biotech's shares have risen nearly sixfold over the past year.
The change will take effect before the market opens on Oct. 9, the stock exchange said in a statement late Thursday.
Shares of Moderna rose 2.4% in premarket trading, adding to a 563% gain over the past 12 months.
The company, which became a household name after it developed one of the first vaccines for Covid-19, surprised the Street last month when an experimental personalized cancer vaccine co-developed with Merck showed positive initial results in its first-ever late-stage trial.
Meanwhile, Warner Bros. is in the process of merging with Paramount Skydance . Paramount has said the merger will close on Oct. 6.
European government bond yields fell on Friday, as they headed for the end of a volatile week that saw yields on various regional securities hit multi-decade highs.

The pan-European Stoxx 600 added 0.3% in early morning trading, with tech stocks leading gains.
Germany's DAX index, up 0.3%, led gains among major regional bourses.
Asian stocks closed mixed on Friday. Japan's Nikkei 225 lost 0.94% to 68,309.46, while the Topix closed 0.99% lower at 4,091.
South Korea's Kospi rose 0.46% to 7,003.74, while the small-cap Kosdaq slid 0.11% to 893.29.

Mainland China markets were closed for a holiday.

articles.title_orig: Home Assistant renames Home Assistant Cloud to Link
articles.title_zh: Home Assistant renames Home Assistant Cloud to Link
articles.content_orig:
﻿Founder Paulus Schoutsen explains why the smart home platform is dropping “cloud” from its name and how a new hub and AI agents could take it mainstream.
﻿Founder Paulus Schoutsen explains why the smart home platform is dropping “cloud” from its name and how a new hub and AI agents could take it mainstream.
The open-source smart home platform Home Assistant is kicking the cloud to the curb — in name at least. “We are renaming Home Assistant Cloud to Home Assistant Link, because we hate clouds,” founder Paulus Schoutsen told The Verge in an interview ahead of today’s announcement . “Big tech ruined the cloud, so we’re out.”
The move is part of a long-term strategy Schoutsen and his team have been pursuing to make Home Assistant a mainstream smart home platform. Schoutsen says most users find the powerful platform after hitting the limits of mainstream options like Google Home, Amazon Alexa, and Apple Home. But it has a steep learning curve, and that’s what he’s looking to change.
I spoke with Schoutsen at the Z-Wave Summit in Boca Raton, Florida, this week about the changes and Home Assistant’s future plans, which include lowering barriers to entry by developing simpler dashboards, making setup more intuitive, and using generative AI to reduce complexity. He also said they plan to launch a new hub next year that’s more user-friendly. “We’re growing up.”
“You don’t have to trust me not to misuse your data because I just don’t have your data.”
Renaming Home Assistant Cloud to Link is mostly symbolic. The features stay the same, aside from some back-end improvements to speed and reliability. The new name also tries to address a concern some new users had that it meant Home Assistant ran in the cloud, says Schoutsen. Home Assistant runs on local hardware and controls your smart home locally, but this means once you leave your home network, you can’t control anything.
For $6.50 a month or $65 a year, Home Assistant Link gives you a convenient way to access your Home Assistant instance from anywhere, alongside the option to enable other internet-dependent features such as integration with Alexa and Google voice control, text-to-speech, speech-to-text, and encrypted backups.
The move addresses an awkward dynamic for the platform. Schoutsen and his team have spent years campaigning against proprietary cloud ecosystems, which he believes hurt the smart home, and encouraging people not to buy cloud-dependent products, all while offering a service with “cloud” in the name. However, unlike some cloud services, Home Assistant Cloud was never mandatory, and you could always replicate everything it provided with other methods; the same remains true for Link.
Schoutsen says Link is also different from many cloud services because it has no access to your data. Link is run by Nabu Casa , Home Assistant’s commercial partner, and all Link traffic is encrypted . “We can’t see it, and we don’t want to,“ he says. “You don’t have to trust me not to misuse your data because I just don’t have your data.” The service provides a revenue stream to fund the platform’s development, with 60 percent of the profit going to the non-profit Open Home Foundation that runs Home Assistant.
For Home Assistant, cloud-dependent products are a hard no. “The cloud is ruining how people think of the smart home,” says Schoutsen, pointing to the recent examples of Nest shutting off the cloud for its early thermostats , smart TVs sending your data to the cloud without you knowing, and Weber sunsetting the June Oven’s servers . “Now you have a dumb oven that cost $1,500. It’s crazy,” he says. “People get so used to it and get so disappointed by it.”
The cloud isn’t all bad, Schoutsen concedes. Speech-to-text, backups, and AI work better online, but the problem is products that stop working without it. He wants product manufacturers to commit to offering local control by default, using open standards (Matter, Zigbee, Z-Wave, MQTT, ESPHome), never locking basic features behind a cloud, and allowing users to control their own data.
“I’d love to see a nutrition label on boxes showing if a product is cloud-dependent or not,” he says, adding that they’re building a database to help consumers find products that aren’t fully reliant on the cloud.
This stance against the cloud is likely to appeal to consumers who are increasingly concerned about who has access to their data. But Home Assistant still has a long way to go before it becomes mainstream. Schoutsen says Home Assistant is installed in an estimated 2.7 million homes, but that’s still a fraction of the reach of Amazon Alexa, Google Home, Samsung SmartThings , and Apple Home. Winning over mainstream users will be hard.
The biggest barrier to entry is complexity. Home Assistant does a lot, meaning you have a lot of choice, which can be overwhelming. “If you want to try something with Home Assistant, the answer is never no,” says Schoutsen. “We want everything to be possible, which means that the UX is more complicated, and that scares people.” In comparison, “You open Apple Home, and there’s like nothing you can do,” he says.
Over the last few years, the team has been working to remove those barriers without taking away functionality. “We’re looking to lower the floor without lowering the ceiling,” he says. There are plans to launch a successor to the Home Assistant Green hub that will be easier to set up. “We want to make it more like onboarding a Philips Hue hub,” says Schoutsen.
They are also working to make the UX easier and will integrate the HACS community store — where users find and install community-built integrations — into Home Assistant next month. This should make integrations easier to find and set up. “If people haven’t tried Home Assistant in over a year, they should give it a shot,” he says.
“We’re looking to lower the floor without lowering the ceiling.”
Another big push that could turn into a major selling point for the platform is a “No Device Left Behind” program . Nabu Casa is developing devices that will more easily bring people’s existing analog or legacy tech into the platform — such as old receivers, AC units, solar panel inverters, even TVs — using technology such as serial , IR, and Modbus .
Schoutsen sees AI as a big driver for Home Assistant. “AI is going to solve the complexity problem, and our biggest weakness is becoming our biggest strength,” he says. As a broad, open platform that can bring together data and controls from across your smart home, Home Assistant could provide a useful foundation for AI agents.
I used Claude to set up Home Assistant last year, and it was a big improvement over trying to figure out what on earth YAML was. “Soon you’re just going to have your agent configure your software for you,” he says. “Because people don’t want the software, they just want the solution that comes out of it.” Schoutsen acknowledges that agents raise obvious privacy concerns, but says Home Assistant keeps your data at home and you can choose which agent to trust with it, including one that runs locally.
Ultimately, Home Assistant may not need to reinvent itself to win over the mainstream if it can become the foundational layer that lets your home talk to your AI agent or platform of choice. “If you just have a box in your house that runs Home Assistant that connects all your data to your agents or to, say, Apple Home, that’s great,” he says. “That’s a win for Home Assistant.”

articles.title_orig: Back in the Saddle: True Waller’s journey from spinal surgery to world champion
articles.title_zh: Back in the Saddle: True Waller’s journey from spinal surgery to world champion
articles.content_orig:
Cleveland junior True Waller didn't let a back injury slow her down from carrying on her family's legacy and giving back to help others.
It's easy to pull into Blythewood Farms and think, this is all just horse play. But what lies beneath the mane is a family legacy that dates back to 1942.
"My great grandmother Bess Neil made this created this farm, and it's been passed down since to my grandma, and my mom and my sister and I are continuing to ride and continuing to kind of keep that dream going," Cleveland High School junior, and junior exhibition horse show world champion, True Waller said.
"It means it means a lot. Yeah, get a little emotional about it, really, but this is you know a pretty amazing place, and it's meant a lot to a lot of people for a lot of years," True’s mother, Key Waller, added.
Given the family tradition, it may be surprising that True Waller's passion was volleyball. Until a back injury changed everything.
"I had three herniated discs in my spine, so I had a spinal discectomy. So, it was spinal surgery, and it was July. I had my surgery July 2025," True said.
"Of course, that was really difficult because you know it's spinal surgery on a 14-year-old," Key said.
Due to her injury, True can't ride on horseback. But like her great grandmother before her, she rides saddle seat. And like her mother and sister, True is now a world champion. What some would call a setback; the Waller family calls fate.
"It's really nice knowing that I could do it myself, and like, obviously, like being in this family is very honoring just because of our ancestry. But being able to honor it as well is very awesome."
Rehabbing from spinal surgery at 14 years old to becoming a world champion, no one said growing up would be easy. But now, True is looking to make things easier for other young athletes rehabbing from injuries through her non-profit Revive and Thrive.
"I just think that giving an opportunity to athletes like that is something that I want to do because I was able to have that opportunity. But not everybody does, and it was something that was super important to me because I experienced it," True said.
Life always has a way of bucking you off course. But it's all about saddling back up towards your true purpose.
"Just being able to share my story, I think, is important because, like, yes, I got out of it, but it wasn't easy, and like I did go through that as well,” True said.
“I think sharing that is important to other athletes. Like they're not alone."

articles.title_orig: World Forest Week: FAO urges greater investment and action for the world's dryland forests
articles.title_zh: World Forest Week: FAO urges greater investment and action for the world's dryland forests
articles.content_orig:
FAO’s Call to Action on Dryland Forests emphasizes that proven solutions for reviving drylands already exist, and the priority is to create the conditions to implement them at scale
Dryland forests provide vital ecosystems, resources and livelihoods for communities around the world.
Rome – Forests and trees in the world's drylands sustain the livelihoods, food security and cultural identity of more than two billion people, yet they remain insufficiently recognized in global climate, biodiversity and land agendas, according to the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO).
FAO’s Call to Action on Dryland Forests was launched today during a High-level dialogue on Dryland forests for food, nutrition and resilience held as part of the 10th World Forest Week, running alongside the 28th Session of the FAO Committee on Forestry (COFO) at FAO headquarters in Rome.
The call urges governments, donors and partners to strengthen the sustainable management, restoration and governance of drylands forests; better integrate them into national climate, biodiversity and land priorities; and significantly increase investment in their conservation and sustainable use. It also proposes a new Dryland Forest Support Accelerator as an enabling platform to speed up implementation, mobilize finance, and strengthen country-driven action at scale.
“Dryland forests are central to our lives, and that of future generations,” said FAO Director-General QU Dongyu in a video message. “Yet dryland forests are often underrecognized, under-monitored and under-financed. This must change.”
Drylands - which are characterized by water scarcity - host forests, woodlands and trees outside forests and cover roughly 41 percent of the Earth's land surface. They also account for 27 percent of global forest area.
Drylands produce high-demand wood and non-wood products, buffer people against drought, and provide one of the most accessible safety nets for the world's poorest households – from fuelwood and fodder to wild foods and medicinal plants. They also underpin the resilience of agrifood systems by supporting livestock, protecting soils and water resources, and providing food and income when crops fail.
But around 25 percent of dryland forest ecosystems are already degraded, driven largely by land-use change including agricultural expansion, urbanization and unsustainable resource extraction. Climate change is compounding these pressures, with longer droughts intensifying water stress and increasing fire risk. These impacts fall heavily on smallholders, Indigenous Peoples, pastoralists and local communities, as well as women and youth.
Dryland Forest Support Accelerator
The Call to Action emphasizes that proven solutions for reviving drylands already exist, and the priority is to create the conditions to implement them at scale.
At the centre of the call is the Dryland Forest Support Accelerator – an FAO-anchored, country-driven platform to help move action beyond fragmented projects. It would support countries in integrating dryland forests into national planning processes – including nationally determined contributions and land degradation neutrality targets – accessing long-term finance, strengthening monitoring, and improving coordination across sectors.
Building on FAO’s experience on drylands, notably through the GEF-7 Dryland Sustainable Landscapes Impact Program and the COFO Working Group on Dryland Forests and Agrosilvopastoral Systems, the Accelerator would organize support around three objectives:  gathering evidence and identifying country needs; supporting the implementation and scaling of proven approaches; and capturing results and lessons to inform future action.
The Call to Action further advises that governments, donors and the Rio Conventions give greater political and financial priority to dryland forests across global environmental processes, including through formal recognition of dryland forests as a priority ecosystem under the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD).

articles.title_orig: Moon World Resorts advances plans for moon-shaped experiential resorts
articles.title_zh: Moon World Resorts advances plans for moon-shaped experiential resorts
articles.content_orig:
Giant spherical destinations are planned across the world
The Moon World Resorts project is now progressing from concept into the design and engineering stages
Moon World Resorts' vision for moon-shaped experiential destinations is moving forwards, with the project now progressing from concept into the design and engineering stages.
The company has selected consulting engineering firm Entuitive to support the development of the spherical resorts from design through construction.
The proposed Moon sites are described as the world's most innovative experiential destinations, and are planned for North and South America, Europe, the Middle East, Asia, Oceania and Africa.
They will integrate hospitality, entertainment, wellness, education, technology, attractions, space training, Earth-based space tourism and more.
Moon World Resorts' vision for moon-shaped experiential destinations is moving forwards Moon
"Entuitive is thrilled to be working with Moon World Resorts on this groundbreaking development that will redefine hospitality industry standards," said Barry Charnish , founding principal at Entuitive.
"It's been a great honour to witness the development of the vision of Moon and now quite exciting to kick off this global initiative.
"Moon's signature true sphere and the surrounding 556-acre masterplan are the types of projects that fuel an engineer’s desire to keep designing and creating to push the limits of the built environment."
Sandra G. Matthews , co-founder and president of Moon World Resorts , said: "Barry has supported Moon World Resorts, the vision behind Moon, since inception."
"Entuitive delivers the structural discipline and building envelope expertise a project of Moon's scale and ambition demands," she added.
"Barry's decades of tall building leadership provides absolute confidence in the entire engineering foundation footprint."
In addition, Moon World Resorts has appointed Toronto-based firm BDP Quadrangle as lead architects across its planned Moon resorts.
"A project of this scale cannot be the product of a single discipline working in isolation; it requires architects, engineers, and specialists working as equals toward a shared vision," said Matthews.
